scenes.narration: Hello, my little friends! Why is it that every rainy season, the river water rises and rushes along? And why did our grandparents build such long, tall dikes? Today, Huy's Story Time will tell you the legend of Son Tinh and Thuy Tinh!

Once upon a time, in the land of Van Lang, the eighteenth King Hung had a daughter named Mi Nuong. She was as pretty as a flower and gentle in her heart. Her father loved her very much. King Hung (happily): "My daughter has grown up. I must find her a truly worthy husband." Mi Nuong (happily): "Father, I will do as you wish."

The king sent messengers to every village. They blew horns to announce that he was looking for a husband for his daughter. The Messenger (shouting): "Hear me, people of Van Lang! King Hung is looking for a husband for Princess Mi Nuong! Whoever is talented, come to the capital!" The Villagers (surprised): "Oh! Which young man will become the king's son-in-law?"

Soon after, two young men came to the capital to ask for the princess's hand. One came down from the mountains, and one came up from the sea. The Villagers (surprised): "Look! Two such handsome young men! They do not look like ordinary people at all!"

The first was Son Tinh, lord of the high Tan Vien Mountain. When he waved his hand to the east, sandbanks rose up in the east. When he waved his hand to the west, rows of hills grew up in the west. Son Tinh (firmly): "Your Majesty, I am Son Tinh of Tan Vien Mountain. I ask to marry Princess Mi Nuong."

The second was Thuy Tinh, lord of the deep waters of the sea. He called the wind, and the wind came. He called the rain, and the rain came. Thuy Tinh (proudly): "Your Majesty, I am Thuy Tinh, lord of the great sea. Only I am worthy of the princess!"

Both young men were talented, and both had magic powers. King Hung sat in his big house on stilts and thought for a long time. King Hung (worried): "Both of them are worthy. How can I choose?" The Minister (firmly): "Your Majesty, please set a condition. Whoever does it first will be chosen."

King Hung (firmly): "Tomorrow, whoever brings the wedding gifts first will take Mi Nuong home as his wife!" The gifts were one hundred trays of sticky rice, one hundred bánh chưng, which are square sticky-rice cakes, and a pair each of nine-tusked elephants, nine-spurred roosters, and nine-maned horses. Thuy Tinh (surprised): "Nine-tusked elephants? Nine-spurred roosters? These are so hard to find!" Son Tinh (firmly): "No matter how hard, I will find them all!"

That night, Son Tinh went back to the mountains and forests. The forests had rare animals and sweet-smelling sticky rice. He gathered all the gifts that very night. Son Tinh (joyfully): "Here are the nine-tusked elephants! The nine-spurred roosters and nine-maned horses are all here too!"

But Thuy Tinh dived all through the deep sea, and those animals lived in the forests and mountains. Thuy Tinh (worried): "Where are the nine-tusked elephants? Where are the nine-spurred roosters? The sea is so wide. Where can I look?"

Early the next morning, while the mist still lay on the land, Son Tinh led his line of gifts to the king's house. The bronze drums rang out, boom, boom. King Hung (joyfully): "Son Tinh came first, and his gifts are complete. I will keep my word and give Mi Nuong to you." Son Tinh (joyfully): "Thank you, Your Majesty!"

According to the custom of the Lac Viet people, everyone ate sticky rice together to celebrate the new husband and wife. Then Mi Nuong bowed to say goodbye to her father. Mi Nuong (sadly): "Father, I will follow my husband to his mountain. Please take good care of your health." King Hung (happily): "Go in peace, my child. Live happily with your husband." Son Tinh took Mi Nuong home to Tan Vien Mountain.

When the sun was high, Thuy Tinh finally arrived with his gifts. But Mi Nuong had already gone to the mountain with Son Tinh. Thuy Tinh (surprised): "What? Son Tinh has already taken Mi Nuong away?" The Minister (firmly): "You came too late. The king's word cannot be changed."
Thuy Tinh (angrily): "I will not accept this! I will chase after them and take Mi Nuong back!" Thuy Tinh was full of rage. He turned back to the sea, ready to fight Son Tinh.

Thuy Tinh called the rain and the wind. The sky turned dark. Thunder boomed and lightning flashed, and the rain poured down like a waterfall. Thuy Tinh (shouting): "Wind, blow! Rain, pour down! Water, rise!"
Thuy Tinh led an army of water creatures. Fish, shrimp, crabs, turtles, and river dragons marched along with the waves. The Water Army (shouting): "Forward! Attack Tan Vien Mountain!"

The water rose over the fields and up to the floors of the houses. The villagers led their buffaloes, carried their children, and ran up the high hills. The Villagers (scared): "The water is rising! Run to the mountain, quickly!" The Boy (scared): "Grandpa, I am so scared!"

The water surged up to the foot of Tan Vien Mountain, as if it wanted to swallow the whole mountain. Mi Nuong (worried): "My husband, the water is so high! What shall we do now?" Son Tinh (firmly): "Do not be afraid. I will protect you and everyone!"
Son Tinh used his magic. He lifted hills one by one and moved mountains row by row, building a strong wall to hold back the flood. Son Tinh (shouting): "Hills and mountains, rise up! Stop the water!"

How strange! As high as the water rose, the hills and mountains rose just as high. Thuy Tinh (angrily): "Hmph! I will make the water rise even higher!" Son Tinh (laughing): "As high as your water rises, my mountain will rise just as high!"

Wild elephants, forest animals, and the mountain people came to help Son Tinh too. The warriors wore feather headbands and carried bronze spears, bronze shields, and crossbows. The General (shouting): "Brothers, raise your crossbows! Protect our mountains and forests!" The Villagers (firmly): "Let us all help Son Tinh!" The crossbow arrows flew, whoosh! The water army fell down and scattered, running away.
The two sides fought for many long months. In the end, Thuy Tinh had no strength left. Thuy Tinh (tired): "I cannot fight any more!" The Water Army (scared): "Retreat! Back to the sea!"
Thuy Tinh had to take his army back to the sea. The flood slowly went down, and the fields appeared again. Thuy Tinh (angrily): "Son Tinh, just you wait! I will come back next year!"

The happy villagers beat the bronze drums, danced, and cheered in front of their stilt houses. The Villagers (joyfully): "Son Tinh has won! Tan Vien Mountain stands strong!" Mi Nuong (happily): "Thank you, my husband, for protecting everyone."

But Thuy Tinh never forgot his anger. Every year, when the rainy season came, Thuy Tinh raised the water to attack Son Tinh again. The Boy (surprised): "Grandpa, why is there so much rain and so much water every year?" The Old Grandfather (tired): "That is Thuy Tinh coming to fight Son Tinh again, my child."
But every time, Thuy Tinh lost and had to take his army back to the sea. Thuy Tinh (angrily): "I lost again! Son Tinh's mountain is so strong!"

Learning from Son Tinh, the people of Van Lang worked together to build dikes along the rivers. Some carried soil in bamboo baskets, and some packed the soil down tight. The Old Grandfather (firmly): "Neighbors, let us build the dike tall and strong together!" The Villagers (firmly): "When we work together, we can stop even the biggest flood!" The Boy (joyfully): "I will carry soil to help everyone too!"

Our ancestors told the story of Son Tinh and Thuy Tinh to explain why there is a rainy and flood season every year. The story also praises the ancient Viet people, who worked together against floods to protect their fields and villages.
Today, Tan Vien Mountain is called Ba Vi Mountain, and it is in Hanoi. The mountain is still green, and white clouds float around its peak all year round.

People built many temples to honor Son Tinh and called him Saint Tan. He is the first of the four immortal saints of the Viet people. Lang Suong Temple in Phu Tho is said to be the first place that worshiped Saint Tan Vien.

In Son Tay, Hanoi, there is the Va Temple. Every year on the full moon of the first lunar month, the villages all around gather happily for a festival, remembering the mountain god who protected the people.

My little friends, keep your promises like King Hung, do not let anger take over like Thuy Tinh, and stand together like the villagers who built the dike. When we work together, we can get through any hard time. If you like this story, please subscribe to Huy's Story Time to hear many more wonderful stories. See you again soon!
